units.title: Roads in the rain: day one.
units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: A-road report, 06:30. Standing water across both lanes at the Brackwater dip, about a hand deep at the kerb. The temporary lights at the junction are dark again, I assume the power went at five, so it's a free-for-all with one man in a hi-vis jacket waving his arms at everyone in turn. He is doing his best. His best is not enough. Allow ten minutes extra, more if you're behind the milk tanker.

units.title: Collections: the outage excuse, again.
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Rope Walk recycling not collected for the third week, and this morning's card through the door says 'operational disruption due to power interruptions'. The bin lorry is diesel. The depot is in Port Ammet, which had its lights on all night. I have rung the council's phone menu and pressed 4, then 2, then 4 again, and been thanked for my patience by a recording. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.title: Kittering Holm: general discussion (part 3).
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Part 2 reached the page limit overnight, so here is part 3. The usual requests apply. Give a source for any claim about the company or the contract. No speculation about named individuals. And please remember that there are real people working on the island in this weather, some of whose families read this board. Thank you.

units.title: Carrow Point station: a wet start
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 07:10 readings. Pressure 996 hPa and falling, 2 hPa in three hours. Wind SE 4 gusting 6. Rain since 02:30, 11.2 mm in the gauge so far. Dew point 8.9, relative humidity 98 percent, visibility about 4,000 m in rain. No fog, and nothing at all on the salt plate. The Met Office says 'heavy at times'. For once they've undersold it.

units.title: Left lift stuck on 4 (again)
units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Left car stuck on floor 4 since seven this morning with its doors half open. The engineer has been 'en route' since ten past seven. The right car smells of the usual. I walked down from 3, which is nothing, before anyone on the upper floors starts telling me about the stairs. When I drove the number 9 we had a breakdown man at the depot who came in four minutes.

units.title: Rain on the lens
units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: Rain all evening here, the sideways kind that comes off the shelf and settles on the lantern glass in beads, each bead carrying a small copy of the light. I wiped the outside panes at midnight with the long squeegee, which is the nearest I come to housework. The beam reaches a little shorter in rain, and the dark beyond it sits a little closer. I counted sweeps until I lost count, then went down for tea.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Same rain at our end of the bay. Three calls in a row asking whether the storm will cut the power. I am a utilities helpline, not a weather god. The script says to 'reassure and log'. Hold music tonight is a pan-pipe version of something that was already sad. Between calls: your squeegee line made me laugh, thank you.

units.title: Back on the road (rested properly this time)
units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Breaker breaker. Been off the board three days, sorry to anyone who wondered. Took my rest at a lit truck stop like a sensible person instead of on the shoulder past mile 212 like a fool. Slept nine hours straight with the cab lights on and the stop's dog barking at the dark the whole time. Coffee here is terrible, which is how you know it's honest. Stretch your legs, drink water, keep it between the lines.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Just asking questions. Why does a company pay a hundred dollars a tree to strip an island bare in thirty days, in the worst month of the year? You don't build a hotel like that. You don't build a data centre like that. You clear everything so you can see anything coming from a long way off. A private refuge for the very rich, bought quietly through an intermediary. Do your research on who has been buying remote land this year. Trimmed for length, full version on my list.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Glad you're back, Merle. Pepper and Duke say hello, and Biscuit the new beagle says nothing because she is asleep upside down. Duke barked when I said your name, but he does that for the vet too. For the record, the back corridor is still a no for Duke after two o'clock. He sits at the turn and looks at me until I go round the long way.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect to see if it were a refuge? Fuel storage applications, a jetty upgrade, a marine licence for a breakwater, power to the island. None of those has been filed. What would we expect to see if it were land speculation? A quiet purchase, a fast clearance, a valuation, then a sale to someone with plans. That is exactly what we see. Buying through an intermediary is ordinary for anyone with money.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: One small correction to the last page of part 2. The camp lights can be seen from Gilliver, not from Lisle; the Lisle shore faces the other way, toward Port Ammet. I mention it only because accuracy is a kindness to the people involved. Also, it is 'fewer lights', not 'less lights'. I know. I can't help it.

units.title: Notice: Gilliver slipway lighting
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: The temporary lighting installed on the Gilliver slipway last week will remain in place permanently, with thanks to Sound Lines for funding the standards. Please remember byelaw 14(2): no access to the slipway after dark except for authorised vessel crews and harbour staff. Anyone fishing from the slip at night will be asked politely to move to the east wall, which is lit and safer. Thank you.

units.title: Gilliver shore lights, last night
units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: For the record: coming into Gilliver last night, 23:52 by the engine room clock, the shore lights browned out. The sodium lamps along the front sank to a dull orange for about forty seconds, then came back. Our new deck floods run off the ship's genset, so for those forty seconds we were the brightest thing on the water by a long way. I'd put money on a feeder trip at the same minute.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Technical note before anyone posts a video. The new slip lights are two 150 W LED heads on the old lamp standard. On a phone camera they flicker at mains frequency, because the camera's shutter is beating against the driver. To the eye they're steady. If your clip shows them strobing, that's your phone, not the lamp, and not anything else either.

units.title: Another night off: freezer questions.
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Three cuts in the night again, which I only know about because the oven clock was flashing and the youngest was standing in my doorway at 3am asking why the landing light went out. Practical questions. 1. Is the freezer still safe after three cuts of about forty minutes? 2. Does Sound Power pay for spoiled food, and how? 3. Is it true the school boiler won't restart after a cut until the caretaker comes in?

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Confirmed. I logged a total failure of shore lighting at 23:52, slipway lights included, with good visibility under the rain. Held off the slip for two minutes until they came back rather than come alongside on our own floods. Nobody on the slip, nobody on the wall. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Is the school bus going through the Brackwater dip or round by the ridge? The last time it flooded they diverted it and nobody told the parents, so half of us stood at the wrong stop in the rain for twenty minutes. The school's text service sent a message about the bake sale instead.

units.title: Has anyone heard from dunlin?
units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Good afternoon all. I notice our young man dunlin has not posted since the middle of last night's session, when he said he was moving to the second position. That is not like him. He usually puts up a tidy summary by lunchtime, with gain settings and the weather. I expect he is asleep or has run out of battery, but I would be glad to hear it from someone. Regards, Ned

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I can see the lights from my front room most evenings now. Last night they were on late, through all that rain, a big one and a small onne beside it. I still dont know whether the young people out there keep a lamp in the window, the way we do. I hope someone has told them about it. It is only manners, but it is nice to know the house is awake.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: A short note rather than a finding. I have spent this week going through registry filings that may relate to Ardent Vale's other holdings, beyond the Holm. I am not ready to post them. Two of the entries do not quite agree with each other and I want to check those first. I know I have been too quick in the past. I will be careful this time.

units.title: Harbour hum clip: the pump was off
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Correction to my post of two days ago. I said I'd found the pump: the circulation pump at the ice plant on the north quay. I asked the plant manager today. The plant was shut for maintenance from the 19th until yesterday, isolated at the board. So the pump was off the night I recorded the clip. That's not it. It's still a pump somewhere. Probably.

units.title: Not arguing (Lisle slip)
units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Ha, anyway. I'm not arguing with Kerris. I said what I saw: shorter than her, about my height maybe, standing right where the slip goes under the water. I was forty metres away in drizzle with my glasses in my pocket. She was on a boat, in fog, with a loud-hailer... Maybe we saw different things. Maybe neither of us saw what we think. It's not a thing I want to win.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: lads the chandlery bait freezer has done its third night of this and the squid is going soft. Sound Power want a form filling in with the times of every cut. if anyone has the times written down post them here and save me guessing. Seth's 23:52 is one

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: good. you're both fine and you're both crew and that's an end of it here. if the height business has to happen at all take it to the Sound Board where they like that sort of thing

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Bus came round the ridge both ways today, I was behind it on the 15:40. Fourteen minutes extra and a lot of children waving at me. Dip still flooded at six. The hi-vis man has been replaced by a portable sign that says ROAD AHEAD, which is technically true of every road.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Still glad I took the hedge job in tollinby. My mate was down at gilliver last night picking up his lad and saw the camp lights through the rain, says one big lamp and a smaller one off to the side like a yard light. Says they were on till he left at half eleven. Hard graft in this weather, fair play to them.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Ferry side, for completeness. The 07:40 was nine minutes late, because apparently rain now counts as 'operational'. The night crossings ran with the new floodlights, which you can see from outside the Lisle shop like a small stadium going past. My neighbour says it puts her off her telly. My neighbour says that about most things.

units.title: Market, wet week
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Langoustine down again at the market. Buyers say the rain keeps the restaurants empty in Port Ammet. Creels came up full of weed on the Holm side this morning, and two lost to the swell off the point. Was hauling late last night when the lights went, aye. Whole coast went brown for a minute. Only lights left on the water were the ferry and the camp.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: bram you lost two last week as well. I've got creels in at cost if you stop feeding them to the Holm side. also put your times in the outage thread for the form, you were out there

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Fair correction. Then not that pump. Quick analysis from the clip you posted: fundamental near 50 Hz with a strong 100 Hz harmonic, and an on-off cycle of roughly 40 seconds. That's mains-driven, and it's a compressor or a thermostat-controlled motor. Anything with a fridge in it qualifies: boats on shore power, the fish market's cold store, a chiller van. List what was plugged in near the quay that night and it narrows quickly.

units.title: Pebble update (she won't go out after dark now)
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: A small update for everyone who helped look for Pebble last month (grey, one white sock, found safe in the Harlands' shed, thank you again Mr Hartley and the girls at number 9). She is eating and purring and lying on the radiator all day. But since about a week ago she won't go out once it's dark. She sits by the cat flap and stares at it. If I open the back door she backs away. Is this normal?

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: On question 1, from the station's power logger: last night's three cuts totalled 2 h 10 min, the longest 52 min. A full freezer with the door kept shut holds for well over a day, so you're fine. A half-empty one less so; fill the gaps with bottles of water. I can't help with 2 or 3, though I'd be surprised if a boiler cared.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Thank you for waiting. When you do post, please put the registry reference and the filing date next to every name. A list without references is just a list. Holding companies hold a lot of things for dull reasons, and the dull reasons are usually in the accounts notes, page twenty or so, under 'investment property'.

units.title: Notice: fire doors (ref KE/DC/0471)
units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Kerrow Estates notice ref KE/DC/0471. Residents are reminded that fire doors on all stair landings must be kept closed at all times. We have received reports of fire doors on floors 6, 7 and 8 being found propped open overnight. Propping fire doors is a breach of the tenancy agreement and a serious safety risk. Self-closing mechanisms will be inspected. We thank residents for their patience and cooperation.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: The only door anyone props in this building is the bin store door on 8, by whoever can't be bothered to walk the bags down properly, and it has been that way since 1989. This notice is about bins. It is not about the hysteria from the upper floors, and I'd thank people not to make it so before they've even read it.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: His car has been in the reservoir car park last night and again tonight. Dark estate, recorder case on the back seat, locked, cold bonnet. I've given the plate to the estate office. If it's still there in the morning I ring it in, simple as that. And for everyone else reading this: the woods are shut to the public after dark for a reason.

units.title: Rain on a caravan roof (for the sleep playlist)
units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on for this one. Forty minutes of rain on my sister's caravan roof, recorded on the binaural head from the bench seat. The awning's on your left, the roof vent drums slightly above and behind you, and there's a gutter overflowing out to the right that comes and goes with the gusts. I needed something gentle this week. Raw file attached, no processing.

units.title: Patrol notes: the rain night
units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Night eight of these. Rain from half two, so no salt fog worth the name, and the insulators got a free wash. Trips still came: 23:51, 01:30 and 03:05, each one logged a section further toward the harbour end of the feeder, same as before. I walked spans 40 to 52 with a lamp at four in the morning. Nothing on the line. No birds, no branches, no flashover marks I could see.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: For your form: Gilliver end trips last night at 23:51, 01:30 and 03:05, each restored by auto-reclose within about a minute except the 01:30, which was 38 minutes because it locked out and someone had to drive to the switch. Seth's 23:52 is the first one, give or take the engine room clock.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: A marine licence can be applied for afterwards, once the clearing is done and nobody is watching. And if it's only land, why hide behind an intermediary at all? Why is the Holm the only island in the Sound being stripped this year? Ferrous always has the boring answer ready. Sometimes the boring answer is the cover story.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I've texted him nine times and rung twice, it goes straight to voicemail, which means the phone's off or dead, not that he's ignoring me, he never ignores me. his car being there is good actually? it means he didn't drive off somewhere. ok that came out wrong. I'm going to stop typing.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Ours did exactly that after a bad fireworks night one year and it took about a month to wear off. Could it be the outages? The streetlight outside goes off with the power and our two hate it, they come in and sit under the table until it's back on.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: A note from me, gently. Please don't speculate in this thread about what has or hasn't happened. If you know dunlin offline, check in with him or his family the normal way. The keeper is dealing with the car properly. People step away from forums for all sorts of ordinary reasons, and I'd like him to be able to come back to a thread that doesn't embarrass him.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: sorry, can't really think about hums tonight. but ok so the 40 second cycle is the thing, isn't it. fridges do that. cold stores don't really, they run long. sorry wetmic, back tomorrow maybe.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Oh, that might be it! Our streetlight has gone off twice this week with the cuts, and the second time Pebble ran under the bed and wouldn't come out for my sister either. Thank you, that's a much nicer explanation than the ones I was making up at midnight. I'll keep the hall lamp on for her.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Agree with the mod. Practical points only. His last post at 01:12 said he was moving to the second position by the outflow. Phones die fast in cold rain, and his always ran the recorder app as well. Somebody who knows him should ring round, and the car gets reported if it's still there. Beyond that, nobody here knows anything, me included.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: I've asked Kerrow which reports they mean and who made them. I'm told the notice is 'routine'. Please don't read anything into it, though I know some of you will, and I know why. If you prop the bin store door on 8, stop. If you didn't, then you didn't. Bev, DCRA

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones off for this one. At the session he mentioned a brother over Tollinby way who 'thinks recording owls is a midlife crisis'. I don't know a surname. If anyone does, that's probably the first call. I'm not saying anything else, the mod's right.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Lads, it's a rich bloke's tax thing. You buy an island, you clear it, you lose money on paper. Nobody's building a bunker in Gilliver. Grow up. Also it's raining so they're probably all in the pub, wherever the pub is out there.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Nice clean file. The roof vent has a resonance around 340 Hz that gives it that drum. Rain on a thin flat aluminium skin is close to ideal broadband noise; it's why caravan holidays put people to sleep. The gutter on the right is the best bit.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Station data for your notes. 31.4 mm since noon yesterday, relative humidity 97 to 99 percent all night, but my salt deposition plate came in clean this morning. Rain scrubs it out of the air. So on last night of all nights, salt fog is about the least likely cause I can offer you. I can't offer you a better one.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Walked the outflow path at dusk with a lamp, gate to gate. Water's over the lower boards by the sluice, which is normal in this rain. Nothing dropped, nothing left. Gate log shows nobody signed in or out. That's all I've got and I'll not have people guessing at the rest.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Observations, not counts. 1. Nobody I know props the doors on 6, 7 or 8. 2. Those three doors had their self-closers adjusted in the spring, per the notice of that time. 3. If the doors are being found open overnight, either a resident opens them or the closers are failing. 4. Item 3 is checkable. I said I have stopped counting. I have. This is just doors.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Thanks. So that's three trip nights I can't put fog against, and one of them in proper rain. I'll stop posting patrol notes after this one, I think, they're getting read in ways I didn't mean. Garvey says hello and that he isn't allowed to say anything else, which he says is the most he's ever been paid for.

units.title: Gate 7 log, wet one
units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: 01:00 patrolled north stack, nil found. 01:40 the fox from the other night on camera 3 again, same limp in the back leg, which I am choosing to find reassuring. 02:10 heavy rain, reefer row alarms twice, reset both. 02:45 patrolled, nil found. Rolls arrived 04:00 courtesy of first_loaf_out's lad on his bike. Good night.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Not to be grim, just practical. The outflow path floods past the sluice in rain like this, and the bank there is clay. If someone goes looking, go in daylight, in boots, with a second person. The rangers know that stretch better than any of us.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Lift engineer came at four, left car working again, right car still smells. Fresh bread arrives at six tomorrow. For anyone on the upper floors who can't face the stairs in the morning, knock on the shop window and I will bring it up in the lift myself. Batteries and torches still at cost price. H

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Speaking as someone who writes these for a living: this is exactly the notice a managing agent sends two or three weeks before a fire risk inspection. Self-closers stiffen in damp weather and stop latching, which is why doors are found ajar. Check the lobby board for an inspection date before anyone reads it as a confession.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I take the lift now. I will say only: the door on 8 by the bin store had no wedge and no prop on Monday, I looked when I took the bags. It was open anyway. Sorry for spelling. I will not comment more on doors.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran
units.text: Last thing from me. I'm closing this account after tonight. Not because of anyone here. My wife says I check this thread more than I check on the kids, and she's right. I won't go into it, any of it, I never could. Davey, you were right to take the hedges. Whoever's out there in this rain: the work ends. It does end.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so for the people asking: we were on a shared voice channel during the session. the last thing in my log from him is 01:14, 'moving to two, back in ten', and then his channel just went to nothing. not static, just nothing, like the app closed. my file runs on for another hour and a half and there's only rain on it. I keep listening to it anyway.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: A fox with a limp is the most reassuring thing anyone has logged on this forum all month. Real animals are consistent. They come back, they limp the same way, they eat the same bins. I'd frame camera 3.

units.title: The chair (an update, sort of)
units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Update on the roof door chair, because people keep asking in the lift (hello, the man from 13 with the beagle). I finally looked at the caretaker's rota on the lobby board: he checks the roof plant room at seven on the morning after the chair moved. So: probably him. I asked him today. He said he 'moves a lot of chairs'. Which is not a no. It is also not a yes. I have drawn him, kindly.

units.title: Cab view, quiet night (no deep questions)
units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: After last week I'm keeping it simple. Wind 9 metres a second and dropping. Two lifts of rebar to level 14, one pallet of blocks. A fox crossing the site road at half twelve (everyone's got a fox this week). The ring road from up here like a necklace somebody dropped. That's it. No questions from me tonight. Have a good shift, all of you.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: lol 'reports of doors being propped open overnight' = someone at kerrow finally found our thread. imagine the meeting. ok, sincerely for one second: the 7 door was open at 2am last week, I shut it behind me on the way down and it was open again when I came back up four minutes later. nobody passed me. could be the closer. probably is.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Welcome back! Terrible coffee needs a terrible pastry to keep it company, so I'd send you a cardamom knot, but it would arrive in about nine days and be a weapon by then. We've got the first rye of the week in and the whole street smells of caraway. Rest is a skill, as my old boss used to say while asleep on the flour sacks.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: can't sleep. going to drive up to the reservoir at first light and walk to position two. I know where it is, I picked it with him. if anyone wants to come, I'll be in the car park by seven.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: lovely post, thank you, Bo. And while I have everyone: the thread from last week stays closed. Please don't start follow-ups to it, and please don't post guesses about who wrote what in it. Company on the night shift, not campfire stories. Drink some water.

units.title: Called it.
units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Three weeks ago I posted that the lights along the coast would start to go out. Nobody listened... Now look at the Sound. Night after night, feeder after feeder, moving toward the water. I'm not saying I'm glad. I'm saying some of us read the signs while everyone else was making jokes about foxes. I've said too much already.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Please don't go alone, and not in the dark. If you go at seven, go with the keeper or with someone from here who knows the path, and tell somebody when you're back. Give it until the estate office has rung the plate in. I'd rather you were tired than in the sluice.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: And another one leaves just before the end. Ask yourselves why the people who worked for Grieve all go quiet at the same point... Watch what happens when the lights on the Holm go out on the 30th. I won't say more here. Some of you know where to find me.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Sorry if this is the wrong place for it. I just wanted to say I thought closing that thread was the right thing, and that you did it kindly. I was one of the people who kept reading it longer than I should have. I won't say anything more about it. Thank you for the rebar and the fox, Bo.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I might be wrong to post this, but I don't think anyone has said it plainly. The camp lights were on through the rain tonight, from about when it got dark, the same as most nights. That's all I wanted to say. Whoever is out there seems to be keeping their hours. Sorry, I know that isn't news.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Housekeeping isn't my job, but the edit history is public. Your post from three weeks ago originally said 'the signal will change'. You edited it on the 22nd, after the outages had started, to read 'the lights along the coast will go out'. The edit is timestamped. That isn't a prediction, it's a correction made after the fact. n of 1, but it's a clear one.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: 'he moves a lot of chairs' is going on a plaque in the stairwell. honestly ivy this is the most reassuring thing that's happened on the cardio of doom all month. a man with a rota. a man with chairs. let him have the chairs.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Fox count from the ward window: one, sitting under the ambulance bay light like it pays rent there. Two admissions, both chests, both grumpy about the hospital tea, both right. Thanks for the necklace, Bo. Back to it.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: Dmitra is right about the edit history, and I've checked it myself. The thread stays up so people can see that for themselves. No pile-on, please. Lamp Hours is company on the night shift, not a court, and nobody needs to be sentenced at two in the morning.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Edits are for clarity. The meaning was always there, for anyone willing to see it... Some people would rather check timestamps than look at what's happening in front of them. That's fine. I know what I wrote and I know what I meant.

units.title: Wet floors and dark streets (porter's log)
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Cheery news from B corridor: the vending machine by X-ray has been fixed and now sells only the orange crisps. A&E had four 'fell over in the dark' cases in before midnight. Two from Gilliver, where the street lights browned out again: one wrist, and one very embarrassed man who walked into his own wheelie bin and wanted that written down accurately. Wet floor signs everywhere. Mop count: three.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: good man merle anyway the rank outside the hospital is lit like a stage these days and the drivers who kip in their cabs between fares all park right under the lamps now, ten of us in a row like ducks, nobody says why and nobody has to

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Source? Oh wait. The source is you, three weeks later, with an edit button. I do a radio show where people ring in after things happen and tell me they knew. Every one of them meant it. None of them had written it down first.

units.title: About the caller (I may have misheard)
units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I owe Orla and everyone a small correction. I've replayed that night in my head too often, which is the trouble with insomnia; you get a lot of rehearsal. The name the caller said, the one I thought sounded like someone on the island crew: I now think it may have been a surname I know from the Tollinby paper, not a first name at all. I may have misheard. I'm sorry for adding to it.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: our yard lights went out four nights running last week and not one of the forty of us thought 'signs', we thought 'scanners won't charge, targets are going to be murder'. which they were. break's over, aisle 41 calls

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: The orange crisps are a test of character, and I'm sorry to hear about the wrist. I hope it's a clean break, if that's something one is allowed to hope for. The wheelie bin man has my sympathy and my respect for wanting the record kept straight.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Thank you. Honestly. For the record, I cut that line because I don't want any real name going out on air at three in the morning, not because of whose it sounded like. Stories grow every time they're retold. Yours just shrank, which is much rarer and much better.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Clean as a whistle, the registrar said, six weeks in a cast. Also: my porter's mate, the one who used to cut trees, told me tonight he's done with the forums. Says it's better for him. I think he's right. He was humming on the morgue run, which I haven't heard him do since I met him.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: A character in one of the old novels on my shelves says that a prophecy is only a guess that happened to be lucky, and a threat is a guess that wants to be. I'd gently ask that nobody make guesses about what happens on the 30th to people who are working out there and can't answer.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Memory of a voice is rewritten each time you replay it, and three in the morning is the worst possible studio. Saying 'I may have misheard' in public is the most honest sentence on this forum this week. That's not me being clinical. That's me saying well done.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Or someone had a word with him. People don't just change their memories after a week... a surname from the local paper, very convenient. Ask who benefits from him taking it back. I've seen this happen before and it always starts with an apology.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: I've removed a reply that suggested a member had been pressured into his correction. He wasn't, and we don't do that to people here. Thank you, awake_at_3_again, for coming back and saying it. That's exactly what this place is for.

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: (He's right, as he annoyingly tends to be. There's a fire risk inspection notice pinned in the lobby for the second of next month. I photographed it at two in the morning, like a normal person, while eating cereal standing up.) So: an inspection. Also, possibly, doors. Both can be true.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: the caretaker moved my bike last year to mop the landing and put it back facing the other way and never said a word so it's very possible love, he's a mover of things, he means well, I've left him a flapjack on the meter cupboard

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: just in love from the depot and the door on 6 was shut tight when I came up which I can tell you for certain because I waited in the lobby for the sky to go grey at the window first like I said I would, and then I went up, and it was shut, and the lights were on, so that's something nice to read at five in the morning
